newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ARS official expects DeBeers deal next year - agency.
newsitem.headline: ARS official expects DeBeers deal next year - agency.

text.p: A senior official with Russian diamond firm Almazy Rossii-Sakha said the Russian government had been dragging its feet on a deal with diamond giant De Beers but said he thought a deal would come in 1997.

Interfax news agency quoted Lev Safonov, first vice president of the company, as saying that if an interim agreement were broken off before a new deal was in place, the two sides would conduct trade under "other conditions".

De Beers officials said Wednesday they were giving the Russian government until the end of 1996 to sign a formal diamond trade agreement and said otherwise the South African firm would terminate its interim agreement.

"We are publicly announcing that if there is no progress by the end of the year, our agreement will terminate on that date," Raymond Clark, general director of De Beers's Russia representation, told a news conference in Moscow.
Safonov said the De Beers announcement had not surprised the company because the government had been slow to finalise a trade agreement.

De Beers controls about three quarters of the world diamond market and Russia accounts for about 25 percent of all rough gems De Beers sells. A five-year deal expired in December 1995 and was replaced by a memorandum signed in Feburay 1996.

The Russian government has dragged its feet for months on signing a deal and De Beers said it had received no official word on the status of a draft agreement presented in October after months of revisions.
